title: Reuse exact canonical SparseTensorEntry evidence digest tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: SparseTensorEntry.evidence_sha256s is bounded to 64 digests and retained as the canonical immutable evidence container, but __post_init__ always routed even an exact already-canonical tuple through _sorted_strings(..., digests=True). That path validates into a list, builds a duplicate-detection set, sorts the list and creates a replacement tuple even when no canonicalization is necessary. Adding an evidence cache, index or parallel representation would increase rather than reduce the surface.
primary_claim: SparseTensorEntry now validates an exact tuple of lowercase SHA-256 digests in one ordered pass and retains that tuple by object identity when it is already strictly sorted and unique. Duplicate or invalid digests remain fail closed, while non-tuple or out-of-order bounded input still uses the existing _sorted_strings canonicalizer. Tensor evidence semantics, Fourfold authority, wire serialization and digest semantics are unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the already canonical immutable evidence tuple instead of introducing a cache, evidence index, adapter or second representation. Keep the existing _sorted_strings path only for inputs that actually require ordering or canonicalization. This removes redundant canonical-path materialization while preserving the single SparseTensorEntry evidence representation and bounded fail-closed contract.
acceptance: an exact canonical evidence_sha256s tuple is retained by object identity after digest, ordering and uniqueness validation
reverse-ordered bounded evidence still canonicalizes deterministically through the existing fallback
oversized evidence fan-in is still refused before element access
invalid and duplicate SHA-256 digests remain fail closed
